 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company assailing the impugned award dated 26.06.2013 passed by Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Biora, Rajgarh (M.P.) in Claim Case No.16/2012, whereby an amount of Rs.3,29,900/- has been awarded in favour of the respondents no.1 to 5, survivors of the deceased Kanhaiyalal.
2.

entities.text: Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Biora, Rajgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that car which met with an accident wherein the deceased was travelling was insured for only private purposes by policy Ex.D-1 which was used for plying on hire.
Therefore, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
The learned Claims Tribunal has not taken into account the aforesaid ground of the Insurance Company and has wrongly saddled the liability on the Insurance Company.
Hence, prays for allowing the appeal by setting aside NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8899 2 MA-413-2014 the impugned award, as far as the liability of the Insurance Company is concerned.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents, survivors of the deceased submits that the Claims Tribunal has not committed any error as there was no evidence available on record that car was given on rent or plied for commercial purpose.
covers risk of occupant of the car and evidence does not prove that it was given on rent.
Therefore, learned Claims Tribunal has not committed any error in saddling the liability for payment of award amount on the Insurance Company.
4. In the light of the aforesaid, the arguments advanced on behalf of the Insurance Company do not impress this Court.
This appeal being devoid of any substance, fails and is hereby dismissed.
